grades.quote: Each page of virtual memory address space maps to an underlying page frame of physical memory or to none.
grades.reason: Explains that mapping is a table at page granularity and that a virtual page can map to a physical frame or to none. This is the core reason unmapped parts of a sparse address space use no physical memory. It never mentions sparse address spaces or the span-versus-usage contrast directly.

grades.quote: The guard page’s PTE is invalid (i.e., PTE_V is not set), so that if the kernel overflows a kernel stack, it will likely cause a page fault and the kernel will panic.
grades.reason: Only incidentally relevant. It shows that some virtual addresses, such as the guard page, are left unmapped with an invalid PTE and so have no physical backing. The passage is about the kernel layout and direct mapping, and it doesn't explain why a sparse address range uses little physical memory.
